en: Vimānavatthu: The Mansion of the Man,
Chapter on the Great Chariot (Mahārathavagga)
6. The Mansion Story of the First Duty "This celestial mansion, with its pillars of jewels,
rises twelve yojanas high on all sides."
Seven hundred magnificent gabled chambers,
beautiful with pillars of beryl and adorned with golden ornaments;
there you eat, drink, and enjoy yourself.
Divine lutes play their sweet melodies; here,
divine flavors and the five strands of sensual pleasure abound,
while women adorned in gold dance.
“By what means is your complexion such as this?
… [as before] … And your complexion illuminates all directions?”
Thus that son of the gods was delighted...
[as before] ...the fruit of which deed this is.
“Meritorious deeds should be performed by the wise person who understands,
while the Buddhas who have reached the right path still remain.”
Wherein what is given bears great fruit.
Truly, for my benefit has the Buddha come from the forest to the village.
Having gained confidence in that,
I went to the Tāvatiṃsa realm; because of that,
my complexion is such as this.
"...and my radiance shines in all directions.
Thus ends the sixth *Vimāna*, the First *Karaṇīya*.
